spots.name: Kherson Art Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kherson Art Museum is an art museum in Kherson, Ukraine. It is housed in Kherson's former city hall building. The museum opened on 27 May 1978.

spots.name: St. Catherine's Cathedral, Kherson

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of St. Catherine is a religious building belonging to the Orthodox faith that is situated within the Kherson fortress, in the city of Kherson, Ukraine. It was built in 1781–1786, one of the earliest churches in New Russia.

names.ja: 聖エカテリーナ大聖堂

spots.name: Antonivka Road Bridge
spots.summary: The Antonivka Road Bridge, also referred to as the Antonivskyi Bridge, is a ruined box girder bridge on the Dnieper river in Kherson, Kherson Oblast, southern Ukraine. It became a flashpoint during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, and was largely destroyed in November 2022.

spots.name: Kherson Local History Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kherson Local History Museum is a cultural institution and museum that was created in 1963 following the merging of the Kherson Historico-Archeological Museum and the Kherson Natural Historical Museum. The Historico-Archeological Museum was founded in 1890 and the Natural Historical Museum was founded in 1899.

spots.summary: Kherson TV Tower was a 199 m (653 ft) tall steel space framed truss communications tower located in the Ukrainian city of Kherson. The building was uniquely built, having been built by using the cross bracing system.

spots.name: Krystal Stadium
spots.summary: Krystal Stadium is a multi-use stadium in Kherson, Ukraine. It is currently used mostly for football matches and is the home of FC Krystal Kherson. The stadium has 3,400 seats and holds 15,000 spectators.
